name: agtiapi_EncryptionIoctl
prose: Handles an encryption-management ioctl for the card; returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS or IOCTL_CALL_FAIL. Precondition: pCard and pIoctlPayload are valid; user blob pointers in the payload are user addresses. It first sets pIoctlPayload->hdr.Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INVALID_CODE, points pCard->ioctl_data at the payload body, reinitializes pCard->ioctl_completion and only prints a warning if encrypted IO is outstanding. It then switches on the minor function: GET_INFO, SET_MODE and DEK_INVALID call the corresponding tiCOMEncrypt* function and store its result in rc; KEK_ADD copies the KEK blob from user space (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if access_ok or copy_from_user fails), calls tiCOMEncryptKekAdd, and if that returned tiSuccess records the KEK in the local table with agtiapi_AddKek (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if that fails, after the chip was already updated); DEK_ADD copies the DEK blob, adds it to the local table (agtiapi_AddDek), maps it to its KEK (agtiapi_MapDekKek) and then calls tiCOMEncryptDekAdd, returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL when a copy or local step fails (leaving earlier local updates in place); KEK_NVRAM sets rc to tiError; DEK_ASSIGN maps the DEKs locally (IOCTL_CALL_FAIL with Status INVALID_CODE on failure) and otherwise sets rc to tiSuccess, skip_wait to 1 and the body status to tiSuccess; ERROR_QUERY clears the query structure, and if no error events are queued and the query flag requests blocking it waits interruptibly (returning IOCTL_CALL_FAIL if interrupted); once events or the non-blocking flag allow it, it sets rc tiSuccess, skip_wait 1 and status tiSuccess; an unrecognized minor function sets Status INVALID_CODE and returns IOCTL_CALL_FAIL. After the switch: rc == tiSuccess waits for pCard->ioctl_completion unless skip_wait is set, then sets hdr.Status to ioctl_data->status; rc == tiNotSupported sets hdr.Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED with no wait; any other rc sets IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_INVALID_CODE with no wait; it then returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS.
note: lxencrypt.c:779-1016. Reviewer 1 right (NOT_SUPPORTED status possible; KEK/DEK adds can leave chip or local state committed: 846-851, 883-896); reviewer 2 right (wait only when rc==tiSuccess and !skip_wait, 998-1004). PARTLY READ: SET_MODE register assembly (800-832) and the error-query queue scan (950-986) via control-flow lines only.

name: ostiInitiatorEvent
prose: Initiator event callback of the FreeBSD adapter; returns void. It switches on eventType. CnxError, TransportRecovery and the default case only print a message. Discovery: sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE in the card flags; for tiDiscOK it sets AGTIAPI_DISC_COMPLETE in the portal status and, unless AGTIAPI_INIT_TIME is set (the test is replaced by TRUE when HOTPLUG_SUPPORT is defined), calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle, sets AGTIAPI_DISC_DONE | AGTIAPI_PORT_LINK_UP and re-arms the IO_timer callout with agtiapi_CheckIOTimeout; for tiDiscFailed it calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle and clears AGTIAPI_DISC_DONE. DeviceChange: calls agtiapi_GetDevHandle unless AGTIAPI_INIT_TIME is set (without HOTPLUG_SUPPORT). TaskManagement: takes the ccb from ((tiIORequest_t *)parm)->osData; if TASK_TIMEOUT is set it frees the TM ccb with agtiapi_FreeTMCCB; otherwise it sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE, for tiTMOK sets TASK_SUCCESS and, for a DEV_RESET ccb whose IO has not completed (startTime != 0), starts a local abort with tiINIIOAbort, and then frees the TM ccb (agtiapi_FreeTMCCB) whatever the event status. LocalAbort: takes the ccb from parm->osData and sets AGTIAPI_CB_DONE for every event status; for tiAbortOK with TASK_MANAGEMENT set it allocates a TM ccb (logging and skipping when none is available), marks it DEV_RESET and issues tiINITaskManagement(AG_TARGET_WARM_RESET), freeing the new TM ccb if that fails, and then frees the abort ccb; tiAbortOK without TASK_MANAGEMENT, and tiAbortFailed (which only logs), leave the abort ccb allocated.
note: osapi.c:48-249. Reviewer 1 mixed: right for abort ccbs (no TASK_MANAGEMENT or tiAbortFailed keeps them, 200, 238-244), wrong for TM ccbs: agtiapi_FreeTMCCB at 187 runs for every non-timeout TM event status. Reviewer 2 right (CB_DONE is set at 194 before the tiAbortFailed test, so it is not only logging). Old prose wrongly said a TM ccb with non-tiTMOK status stays allocated. Not read: agtiapi_GetDevHandle and agtiapi_FreeTMCCB bodies; exact TM-failure sub-branches (169-185) only logging seen.

name: lp_intr
prose: Receive interrupt handler of the PLIP parallel-port network interface; returns void. Precondition: the caller holds the ppbus lock (asserted with ppb_assert_locked) and arg is the lp_data. It handles one received frame in one of two modes. With IFF_LINK0 set it reads length bytes and then the frame with clpinbyte; otherwise it reads nibbles while the LPIP_SHAKE status bit is set (if that bit is initially clear it returns after the loop without doing anything). A timeout, a bad or oversized length, a missing/short frame (not longer than the header) all go to the error label err. For a frame longer than the header it clears sc_iferrs, subtracts the header length and increments IFCOUNTER_IPACKETS by 1 and IFCOUNTER_IBYTES by the payload length, both before calling m_devget; if m_devget returns a mbuf it releases the ppbus lock, calls lptap, sets the FIB and queues the packet to netisr (NETISR_IP), then retakes the lock; if m_devget returns NULL nothing is queued, no error is counted, and the function still returns with the lock held. The err label writes 0 to the data register, increments IFCOUNTER_IERRORS and sc_iferrs, and when sc_iferrs exceeds LPMAXERRS prints a message, writes 0 to the control register, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and resets sc_iferrs to 0. The lock is held again on every return.
note: if_plip.c:521-654. Reviewer 1 right (m_devget failure queues nothing and counts no error: 574-584, 626-637); reviewer 2 right (IPACKETS/IBYTES and iferrs reset precede m_devget: 567-573, 619-625). Gotos to err at 538,542,545,552,560,565,596,610,617; returns 584, 637, fall-through after err at 654. 'every return' = the three exits listed.

name: ppb_peripheral_negociate
prose: Peripheral-side IEEE 1284 negotiation; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the caller holds the ppbus lock; mode is a mode ppb_request_mode accepts (another mode panics there). It sets the bus mode to PPB_COMPATIBLE and the 1284 state to PPB_PERIPHERAL_NEGOCIATION, computes request_mode, then spins up to 10 iterations (1 us delay each) while nBUSY is set. If the SELECT status line is not set or the spin ran out it sets error ENODEV and goes to the error label without calling ppb_1284_set_error. Otherwise it reads the data register r: if r equals the requested mode byte or NIBBLE_1284_NORMAL it drives the control lines; for NIBBLE_1284_NORMAL it calls ppb_1284_set_error(PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED) and takes the error label with EINVAL; for any other matching byte it sets the state to PPB_PERIPHERAL_IDLE, switches the ppbus mode to PPB_BYTE only when r is BYTE_1284_NORMAL (other accepted modes leave the mode at PPB_COMPATIBLE) and returns 0. If r matches neither, it drives the control lines, latches PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED through ppb_1284_set_error (recorded only if no error was already latched and the state is not already PPB_ERROR) and takes the error label with EINVAL. The error label calls ppb_peripheral_terminate(bus, PPB_WAIT) and returns the error code.
note: ppb_1284.c:196-272. Reviewer 1 right (only BYTE_1284_NORMAL switches the mode, 241-243); reviewer 2 right (ENODEV path 213-215 does not call ppb_1284_set_error; only the EINVAL paths do, 235, 259). Old prose wrongly said both error paths latch PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED. Not read: ppb_peripheral_terminate details beyond its call.

name: ppb_1284_negociate
prose: Host-side IEEE 1284 negotiation; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: bus is the ppbus device; mode is one of PPB_NIBBLE, PPB_PS2, PPB_ECP, PPB_EPP (another mode panics in ppb_request_mode, or in the final switch). It first terminates a peripheral-side negotiation if the state is at least PPB_PERIPHERAL_NEGOCIATION, terminates the 1284 link if the state is not PPB_FORWARD_IDLE, sets the bus mode to PPB_COMPATIBLE, resets the error to PPB_FORWARD_IDLE, writes the requested mode byte and drives the handshake lines. If the status-line wait for the peripheral's response fails it records PPB_NOT_IEEE1284 and returns ENODEV; if the nACK wait times out it records PPB_TIMEOUT and returns EBUSY; each of these goes through the error label, which calls ppb_1284_terminate and returns the code. If options has PPB_EXTENSIBILITY_LINK set it calls ppb_1284_terminate and returns 0 without entering any of the mode states below. Otherwise it checks the peripheral's answer lines (for NIBBLE and otherwise): a mismatch records PPB_MODE_UNSUPPORTED and returns ENODEV via the error label. On success it sets the state to PPB_REVERSE_IDLE for PPB_NIBBLE and PPB_PS2; for PPB_ECP it sets PPB_SETUP, drives the control lines and waits for the ECP status lines (a timeout records PPB_TIMEOUT and returns ENODEV via the error label), then sets PPB_ECP_FORWARD_IDLE; for PPB_EPP it sets PPB_EPP_IDLE. Finally it sets the bus mode to mode and returns 0.
note: ppb_1284.c:654-805. Reviewer 1 right (PPB_EXTENSIBILITY_LINK: terminate and return 0, 740-743); reviewer 2 wrong in effect: PPB_SETUP at 767 is only an intermediate state, the success state for ECP is PPB_ECP_FORWARD_IDLE (788), set only after the wait at 772-785 passes. Errors: ENODEV 711, 719, 748, 754, 775, 782; EBUSY 734.

name: ppb_MS_microseq
prose: Interprets a ppbus microsequence; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the caller holds ppb->ppc_lock (mtx_assert). If ppb->ppb_owner is not dev it returns EACCES. Otherwise it loops over the microinstructions starting at msq: MS_OP_PUT or MS_OP_GET looks up the transfer description with mode2xfer; when it has no loop sequence, a PUT writes arg[1] bytes from arg[0] with PPBUS_WRITE and returns that call's error if nonzero, and a GET panics; when it has a loop sequence the function runs the internal init sequence and then the loop sequence by recursive calls, returning the error from either if nonzero. MS_OP_RET stores arg[0].i in *ret when ret is non-NULL and returns 0. Any other opcode is executed by PPBUS_EXEC_MICROSEQ on the parent bus, which may advance the instruction pointer, and a nonzero error is returned. It does not itself construct a sequence from an opcode (that is ppb_MS_exec).
note: ppb_msq.c:255-344; packet name ppb_MS_exec is wrong, slice 261-344 is ppb_MS_microseq (ppb_MS_exec starts at 137). Reviewer round 15 right (executes caller-supplied msq and can return EACCES, 273-275). The old prose described ppb_MS_exec and was not about this function. Not read: mode2xfer, PPBUS_EXEC_MICROSEQ bodies.

name: puc_bfe_attach
prose: Attach routine of the puc multi-port serial/parallel bus front end; returns 0 or an errno. It sets every BAR's b_rid to -1 and initialises the ioport, iomem and irq resource managers in turn; if one rman_init fails it finalises the ones already initialised and returns that error at once (before any allocation or the fail label). It then gives the rmans description strings, reads the port count with puc_config(PUC_CFG_GET_NPORTS) (a nonzero error is only KASSERTed, not returned), allocates the zeroed sc_port array with M_WAITOK, manages the irq region 1..nports, and runs puc_config(PUC_CFG_SETUP). For each port it sets p_nr, queries type, BAR rid (puc_get_bar returning NULL gives ENXIO), offset and length, tries to reserve the port's register range (a NULL p_rres is not an error: only when it is non-NULL is its bus handle and tag set from the BAR subregion), reserves an irq entry (NULL gives ENXIO), reads the clock and adds a child device, setting its ivars if the child was created. A failed rman_manage_region, puc_config call, puc_get_bar or irq reservation jumps to fail, which deletes the children, releases each port's p_rres and p_ires and each BAR resource, finalises the three rmans, frees their descriptions and the port array and returns the error. After the ports it reads PUC_CFG_GET_ILR (error goes to fail), allocates the shared IRQ resource and sets up the interrupt handler, first as a filter handler (setting sc_fastintr on success) and retrying as an MPSAFE ithread handler on failure; if the interrupt cannot be set up it releases the IRQ and, with no IRQ resource, sets sc_polled. It then probes and attaches each child that exists, deleting and clearing any child whose device_probe_and_attach fails, calls bus_teardown_intr if sc_serdevs is 0 (this call is not conditioned on sc_ires being non-NULL), and returns 0.
note: puc.c:210-398 (slice 257-512 starts inside the function; packet name 'puc_bfe_attach' is correct, slice cut the head). Reviewer round 15 right (p_rres may be NULL without failure, 298-305; GET_NPORTS is only KASSERTed, 257-258); reviewer round 17 right (GET_NPORTS failure not routed to fail). Old prose wrongly listed GET_NPORTS failure under the fail path and said the rman_init failure leaves 'nothing else allocated' (correct) but treated rman_manage_region failure like it; fail path described now exactly. Returns 244, 373, 397.

name: LacSymKey_KeyGenSslTls_GenCommon
prose: Common path that builds and submits a QAT SSL3/TLS/HKDF key-derivation request; returns a CpaStatus. Parameters: instance handle, callback and its tag, lacCmdId (SSL3 derive, TLS v1.1/v1.2/v1.3 derive, HKDF extract/expand/label variants), the op data, hashAlgCipher and the output flat buffer. If pKeyGenCb is NULL it returns LacSymKey_SslTlsSync(...) (the synchronous wrapper) without doing anything else. Otherwise it takes a cookie from pService->lac_sym_cookie_pool: a NULL result gives CPA_STATUS_RESOURCE (after a log message) and the retry marker gives CPA_STATUS_RETRY (cookie set to NULL). With a cookie it stores the instance, callback, tag, op data and output pointers in it, builds a nested-mode hash setup (SSL3: SHA1 inner, MD5 outer and digest size of MD5 with empty prefixes; TLS v1.1 and v1.2 and the HKDF cases choose the hash and secret/label prefix lengths from the op data, handling a pre-master secret longer than the fixed maximum by computing the hash key through computeHashKey when precompute applies), initializes the content descriptor (LacSymQat_HashContentDescInit), and populates the request header, mid and footer for the selected protocol: SSL3 uses LacSymQat_KeySslRequestPopulate and KeySslKeyMaterialInputPopulate (a user-defined label whose virtual-to-physical translation is 0 sets CPA_STATUS_FAIL after a log message); TLS v1.1/1.2 use the hash-state, prefix/AAD and request-parameter helpers and LacSymQat_KeyTlsRequestPopulate (with the same label translation check giving CPA_STATUS_FAIL); HKDF extract/expand/label use the HKDF variants and a switch on hashAlgCipher for the cipher constants. A zero physical address of the output buffer sets CPA_STATUS_FAIL. If status is still CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS it writes the content descriptor header, common header and mid, and submits the message with icp_adf_transPutMsg on pService->trans_handle_sym_tx, taking its status. If the final status is not CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS and a cookie was obtained it frees the cookie with Lac_MemPoolEntryFree. It returns the status.
note: lac_sym_key.c:1182-2087; the packet name LacSymQat_KeyGenSslTlsPopulateRequest does not exist anywhere in the tree, the slice 1351-1605 is the middle of LacSymKey_KeyGenSslTls_GenCommon, so fixed under the real name. Old prose (dropped item) wrongly described a function returning FAIL only on label translation and 'continuing population' after it. PARTLY READ: the per-protocol request population (1300-1990) was read through control-flow lines and call names only; hash algorithm secret-length checks (1296-1440) and the precompute branch (1441-1484) not read line by line; the final cookie-free condition (2073-2084) is inferred from status != CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS.

name: check_accel_unit_config
prose: Validates the configured accelerator-unit split for a c4xxx device; static int, returns 0 or an errno. Parameters are the counts of cy, dc and inline accel units (u8). It reads the ADF_SERVICES_ENABLED value from the general section and returns EFAULT, without printing anything, if that read fails. It then splits the value into service tokens: each token that starts with the CY, SYM, ASYM, DC or INLINE service name ORs the matching service bit into a local service mask (for 'asym' only when num_inline_au is less than the total number of units, so 'asym;inline' with all units inline does not set the crypto bit) and ORs in the result of check_svc_to_hw_capabilities, which prints a message and returns EPERM when the hardware lacks the capability; tokens that match none of these names are ignored. If any capability check failed it prints a message and returns EFAULT. It then returns EFAULT (with printed messages) if dc units are configured but the compression bit is not in the mask, if cy units are configured but the crypto bit is not, or if inline units are configured but the inline bit is not. After those three checks pass it stores the mask in hw_data->service_mask; the later checks can still return EFAULT after that store: the sum of the three unit counts differing from get_num_accel_units, or a zero cy, dc or inline unit count when the corresponding service bit is set (messages printed). Otherwise it returns 0.
note: adf_c4xxx_hw_data.c:1495-1641 (packet name 'unnamed_service_config_validator'; real function is check_accel_unit_config, slice 1524-1784 spans it and later functions). Returns 1511 (no printf, reviewer right), 1575, 1584, 1593, 1600, 1611, 1621, 1629, 1637, 1640. service_mask store at 1603. Reviewer round 17 right (initial config read failure returns EFAULT without a message). Not described: get_accel_unit_config (1644) which is a separate function.

name: ecore_hw_lock
prose: Takes a hardware resource lock through the PF's lock register; returns an ecore status. Parameters: p_hwfn, p_ptt, resource (bit mask) and block. The lock register address is MISCS_REG_DRIVER_CONTROL_0 plus rel_pf_id times the register size. It reads the register; if the resource bit is already set it logs a notice and returns ECORE_BUSY without writing a request. Otherwise it writes the resource to the register at +4 bytes (the lock request) and polls the register up to HW_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES times: if the resource bit is set it returns ECORE_SUCCESS immediately, leaving the request in place, so the lock is held; if the bit is not set and block is false it sets ECORE_BUSY and leaves the loop after the first poll; otherwise it sleeps 5 ms and polls again. If the loop ran to HW_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES it logs a notice and sets ECORE_TIMEOUT. After a non-success loop exit (non-blocking miss or timeout) it writes the resource to the register at the base address (clearing the pending request) and returns the saved status (ECORE_BUSY or ECORE_TIMEOUT).
note: ecore_hw.c:464-518. Reviewer round 15 wrong on the block parameter (it exists, line 467, and non-blocking mode breaks out of the poll loop at 501-503), right that ECORE_BUSY also occurs on the first non-blocking miss; reviewer round 17 wrong: the clearing write at 516 is reached only after the loop breaks or times out, the success path returns at 499 without it. Old prose was correct as written. Returns 488, 499, 518.

name: ecore_iwarp_mpa_complete
prose: Handles the firmware's MPA handshake completion for an iWARP endpoint; static void. Precondition: ep is valid; on RDMA_RETURN_OK ep->qp is used and so must be non-NULL. It sets params.event to ECORE_IWARP_EVENT_ACTIVE_COMPLETE for an active endpoint and ECORE_IWARP_EVENT_PASSIVE_COMPLETE otherwise; for an active endpoint whose mpa_reply_processed is false it parses the private data first; it sets params.cm_info to &ep->cm_info and params.ep_context to ep. A passive endpoint whose state is not ECORE_IWARP_EP_MPA_OFFLOADED logs an error, has its state set to ECORE_IWARP_EP_CLOSED and returns with no callback and no further cleanup; a passive endpoint whose state is ECORE_IWARP_EP_ABORTING returns at once with its state unchanged and no callback. Otherwise it sets ep->state to ECORE_IWARP_EP_CLOSED and switches on fw_return_code: RDMA_RETURN_OK copies cm_info.ord and ird into the QP's max_rd_atomic_req and max_rd_atomic_resp, moves the QP to RTS with ecore_iwarp_modify_qp, sets ep->state to ECORE_IWARP_EP_ESTABLISHED and params.status to ECORE_SUCCESS; MPA timeout gives ECORE_TIMEOUT; reject, FIN, insufficient IRD, RTR mismatch, invalid packet, local error and terminate give ECORE_CONN_REFUSED; MPA reset and any other code give ECORE_CONN_RESET. It then calls ep->event_cb(ep->cb_context, &params) if it is non-NULL. For a non-OK fw_return_code it sets ep->tcp_cid to ECORE_IWARP_INVALID_TCP_CID and then either, for a passive endpoint with no QP, returns the endpoint with ecore_iwarp_return_ep, or removes the endpoint's list entry from the iWARP ep_list while holding iw_lock (spin lock, released after the removal).
note: ecore_iwarp.c:1185-1307. Reviewer 1 right (ABORTING returns early without setting CLOSED, 1219-1221); reviewer 2 wrong: the non-OK branch removes the entry from ep_list (OSAL_LIST_REMOVE_ENTRY at 1301-1303), it does not push to a list; ecore_iwarp_move_to_ep_list is a different function. Not read: ecore_iwarp_return_ep and ecore_iwarp_modify_qp bodies.

name: ecore_ll2_acquire_connection
prose: Acquires a free LL2 connection slot and sets it up; returns an ecore status. Precondition: cxt is the ecore_hwfn and data points to a valid acquire-data structure. It returns ECORE_INVAL, with no side effects, if data->p_connection_handle is NULL or p_hwfn->p_ll2_info is NULL. It scans the slots 0..ECORE_MAX_NUM_OF_LL2_CONNECTIONS-1, taking each slot's mutex around the test, and marks the first slot with b_active clear as active; if all are active it logs and returns ECORE_BUSY. It copies data->input into the slot; for a tx_dest value other than NW, LB or DROP it returns ECORE_INVAL at that point, leaving the slot marked active (it is not released). Otherwise it translates tx_dest, sets main_func_queue to false for the OOO connection type or a secondary queue and true otherwise, defaults tx_max_bds_per_packet to CORE_LL2_TX_MAX_BDS_PER_PACKET when 0 and clamps it to that value otherwise, then installs the callbacks, acquires the Rx, Tx and OOO resources in that order (each failing step logs and goes to q_allocate_fail). It registers the Rx and Tx completion callbacks (the OOO ones for the OOO type) with ecore_int_register_cb when rx_num_desc or tx_num_desc is nonzero, stores the slot index in *data->p_connection_handle and returns the final rc, which is ECORE_SUCCESS at that point. q_allocate_fail calls ecore_ll2_release_connection for the slot and returns ECORE_NOMEM regardless of which step failed. No slot mutex is held at return.
note: ecore_ll2.c:1243-1364. Reviewer round 15 wrong on both points: the invalid tx_dest case is a plain `return ECORE_INVAL` (1289), it does not go to the release path, and every failure after slot selection returns ECORE_NOMEM (1363); the old prose was correct on those. The original-round remark (no contract) is not a prose issue. Not read: ecore_ll2_set_cbs, the acquire_connection_rx/tx/ooo bodies, ecore_ll2_release_connection.

name: qlnx_tpa_start
prose: Handles a TPA (LRO) start completion on a receive queue; returns void. Precondition: cqe is a TPA start CQE for rxq and the ring slots used below hold posted buffers. If cqe->tpa_agg_index is >= ETH_TPA_MAX_AGGS_NUM it increments fp->err_rx_tpa_invalid_agg_num and returns with the rings untouched. Otherwise it syncs and takes the mbuf mp at sw_rx_ring[sw_rx_cons]. If mp is NULL it increments err_rx_mp_null, advances sw_rx_cons by one and returns without changing agg_state. If the CQE parse flags carry CQE_FLAGS_ERR it increments err_rx_hw_errors, reuses the buffer with qlnx_reuse_rx_data, increments IERRORS and returns. If qlnx_alloc_rx_buffer fails it increments err_rx_alloc_errors and IQDROPS, swaps the current buffer into tpa_info[agg_index].rx_buf and the old tpa buffer into the ring slot at sw_rx_prod, produces and consumes one rx BD, reuses a slot for each nonzero entry of ext_bd_len_list, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and returns. If tpa_info[agg_index].agg_state is not QLNX_AGG_STATE_NONE it increments IQDROPS, frees a previously stored mpf chain, stores mp as mpf with mpl NULL, advances the ring, reuses a slot per nonzero ext_bd_len_list entry, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and returns. Otherwise it consumes the rx BD, then for each nonzero ext_bd_len_list entry takes the next ring mbuf (a NULL mbuf or a failed refill frees the chain built so far, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_ERROR and skips that entry) and chains the good ones. If agg_state is still not QLNX_AGG_STATE_NONE at that point it increments IQDROPS, stores mp as mpf (mpl NULL) and returns. Otherwise it records placement_offset, sets mp's length and links the extension chain (mpf = mp with mpl the chain tail, or mp alone), sets M_PKTHDR, rcvif, flowid = rss_hash and the hash type (RSS IPv4, TCP IPv4, IPv6, TCP IPv6, otherwise M_HASHTYPE_OPAQUE), csum_flags CSUM_IP_CHECKED|CSUM_IP_VALID|CSUM_DATA_VALID|CSUM_PSEUDO_HDR with csum_data 0xFFFF, the VLAN tag and M_VLANTAG when the CQE has one, sets agg_state to QLNX_AGG_STATE_START and returns.

name: qla_sec_to_hz
prose: Static inline helper in qla_os.h that converts a number of seconds into scheduler ticks; returns int. It builds a struct timeval with tv_sec = sec and tv_usec = 0 and returns tvtohz() of it. By the kernel's tvtohz: a negative sec gives 1; a value at or above tick_seconds_max gives INT_MAX; otherwise the result is the tick count for that time plus one (so sec == 0 gives 1, not 0). It takes no locks and touches no other state.
note: qla_os.h:110-118; tvtohz at kern_clock.c:592-615 (tv_sec < 0 returns 1; tv_sec >= tick_seconds_max returns INT_MAX; else TIME_TO_TICKS(...) + 1). Reviewer round 1 wrong (tvtohz does clamp to INT_MAX, 608-609); round 2 right (INT_MAX, not negative); round 15 right (sec == 0 does not give 0: the result carries the +1 at 612; I did not evaluate TIME_TO_TICKS exactly). Contract left empty because tvtohz is not an integer-only helper.

name: ql_parse_template
prose: Walks the firmware minidump template and captures each entry into the minidump buffer; static int that returns 0. It reads the template header from ha->hw.mdump_template and records sane_start when the header entry_type is TLHDR. It sets template_hdr->saved_state_array[QL_OCM0_ADDR_INDX] to the template's own ocm_window_array[ha->pci_func] (the template header's array, not ha->hw), saved_state_array[QL_PCIE_FUNC_INDX] to ha->pci_func and template_hdr->driver_capture_mask to ha->hw.mdump_capture_mask. It then visits num_of_entries entries starting at first_entry_offset, advancing by each entry's entry_size: an entry whose entry_capture_mask does not intersect the capture mask gets QL_DBG_SKIPPED_FLAG in driver_flags and is skipped; an entry whose entry_capture_size is nonzero and would not fit in the remaining buffer (buff_level + size > hw.mdump_buffer_size) is flagged skipped and skipped. Otherwise by entry_type: RDNOP does nothing; RDEND increments sane_end; RDCRB, POLLRD, POLLRDMWR, L1DAT/L1INS, RDOCM, RDMEM, BOARD/RDROM, RDMUX, RDMUX2 and QUEUE call their read helper to write into mdump_buffer at buff_level, then apply ql_entry_err_chk and advance buff_level by the returned size; L2ITG/L2DTG/L2DAT/L2INS call ql_L2Cache and, if it returns -1, flag the entry skipped without advancing, otherwise handle it like the other read helpers; CNTRL calls ql_cntrl and flags the entry skipped when it returns nonzero; unrecognized types are flagged skipped. After the walk it prints a 'Template configuration error' message with device_printf if sane_start is 0 or sane_end is greater than 1, and then returns 0 (its only return statement).

Reviewer round 1 right (L2Cache -1 and CNTRL failure paths 4738-4743, 4799-4801); round 2 right (RDNOP does nothing 4704-4705); round 15 right (OCM window read from template_hdr->ocm_window_array 4652-4653). name: qls_mbx_cmd
prose: Sends a mailbox command to the QLogic 8100-series MPI and waits for the reply; returns 0 or nonzero (-1 or a register-access error). ret starts as -1. It reads Q81_CTL_HOST_CMD_STATUS and, if the HTR interrupt bit is set, prints a message and goes to the exit with -1. It then takes the NIC-receive process-address semaphore with qls_sem_lock (failure prints a message and exits with -1 without unlocking), clears mbx_done, writes the i_count command words through qls_mbx_wr_reg (a failed write prints, releases the semaphore and exits with that nonzero error), sets the host-to-RISC interrupt bit, releases the semaphore, sets ret to -1 and clears mbx_done again. It then polls up to 50 iterations. With interrupts disabled (ha->flags.intr_enable == 0) each iteration checks the PI bit in Q81_CTL_STATUS (if clear it sleeps 100 ms and continues); otherwise it reads mailbox register 0: a value with high nibble 0x4000 is a command response, stored in out_mbx[0] with out_mbx[1..o_count-1] read with qls_mbx_rd_reg (a failed read prints and leaves its nonzero error in ret) and the loop is left; a value with nibble 0x8000 is an asynchronous event: the poll count is reset to 50 and the RTH interrupt is cleared; any other nibble just continues polling. With interrupts enabled it checks ha->mbx_done each iteration and, when set, copies ha->mbox[1..o_count-1] into out_mbx[1..o_count-1] (out_mbx[0] is not written), sets ret to 0 and leaves the loop. After each iteration that does not exit it sleeps 1000 ms. If the polling ends by exhaustion, ret holds the last status assigned, so it may be 0 (a register read that succeeded with an unrecognised nibble or after an event) with out_mbx not filled, or -1. At the exit label, when interrupts are disabled it clears the RTH interrupt, and when ret is nonzero it sets ha->qla_initiate_recovery to 1; it returns ret.
note: qls_hw.c:2131-2237. Reviewer round 1 right (returns 0 without filling out_mbx for other nibbles); round 15 first claim right (timeout can return 0 also after 0x8000), second claim wrong: a failed response read breaks out of the for loop (2201) and then out of the while loop (2205) with ret still nonzero, it is not overwritten. Returns: single return at 2237. Not read: qls_sem_lock, qls_mbx_rd_reg/wr_reg bodies.

name: rt2560_prio_intr
prose: Handles completed entries of the rt2560 priority (management) transmit ring; static void, called from the interrupt path with the softc lock held by the caller (the function itself neither takes nor releases it). It first syncs the descriptor map for POSTREAD, then loops from sc->prioq.next: it stops at the first descriptor whose RT2560_TX_BUSY flag is set or whose RT2560_TX_VALID flag is clear. For each finished entry it prints a debug message for success, success-after-retry and too-many-retries results (DPRINTFN only), and uses device_printf for RT2560_TX_FAIL_INVALID, RT2560_TX_FAIL_OTHER and any other result; it syncs the data map POSTWRITE and unloads it, takes the mbuf and node out of the entry (setting data->m and data->ni to NULL), clears RT2560_TX_VALID in the descriptor, decrements prioq.queued, advances prioq.next modulo RT2560_PRIO_RING_COUNT, calls ieee80211_process_callback with the failure bits when the mbuf has M_TXCB set, frees the mbuf with m_freem and releases the node with ieee80211_free_node. After the loop it syncs the descriptor map for PREWRITE, sets sc->sc_tx_timer to 0 when both prioq.queued and txq.queued are 0, and calls rt2560_start(sc) when prioq.queued is below RT2560_PRIO_RING_COUNT. Returns void.

Old prose wrongly said device_printf is used for failure results: only FAIL_INVALID/FAIL_OTHER/default use it (1036-1041); and the claim that rt2560_start may drop the lock was not checked (rt2560_start body not read) so it is removed.

name: rt2860_init_locked
prose: Brings up an rt2860 wireless device; static void. Precondition: the caller holds the RAL lock (RAL_LOCK_ASSERT; the function neither takes nor releases it). If the board has a hardware radio switch that reads off, it only prints a message (the stop-and-return is under #ifdef notyet). It disables DMA, resets DMA indexes and the PBF, loads the 8051 microcode with rt2860_load_microcode and, if that fails, prints a message, calls rt2860_stop_locked and returns. It then writes per-rate TX power registers, waits up to 100 ms for the TX/RX DMA busy bits to clear (timeout: rt2860_stop_locked and return), programs the default MAC registers, sets RT2860_PCIE in sc->sc_flags when the PCI_CFG register shows a non-PCI bus, waits for the MAC to become ready (timeout: rt2860_stop_locked and return), calls rt2860_bbp_init (nonzero: rt2860_stop_locked and return), waits for DMA idle again (timeout: stop and return), initializes RF with rt5390_rf_init for mac_ver >= 0x5390 or rt3090_rf_init for mac_ver >= 0x3071 (a nonzero return from rt3090_rf_init: stop and return), configures antenna chains, then calls rt2860_txrx_enable (nonzero: stop and return). On the success path it clears pending interrupts, sets INT_MASK to 0x3fffc, sends the power-save level command when RT2860_ADVANCED_PS is set, sets RT2860_RUNNING in sc_flags and arms the watchdog callout (hz ticks, rt2860_watchdog); on each failure path above RT2860_RUNNING is not set and the watchdog is not armed.

Old prose omitted the microcode-load failure path and said the failures listed 'either DMA-engine busy timeout, MAC-busy timeout...' (accurate) but also described RT2860_RUNNING being cleared by rt2860_stop_locked, which was not read here. PARTLY READ: register programming (3855-4040) skipped.

name: fxrng_event_processor
prose: Mixes one harvested entropy event into the FenestrasX pools; void. Precondition: event->he_size <= sizeof(he_entropy) (ASSERT_DEBUG only). first_time is true when he_size > 0 and this is the first observation of the source (atomic test-and-set of its bit in fxrng_seen). On first_time it takes FXENT_LOCK and the root BRNG lock; if the root BRNG generation is greater than 0 it releases FXENT_LOCK and calls fxrng_brng_src_reseed(event), which handles the BRNG lock, and returns; otherwise it unlocks the BRNG, hashes the event counter and entropy into pool 0, for a high-quality source adds he_size to fxrng_preseed_ent only if the addition would not overflow ULONG_MAX (it skips the addition on overflow rather than saturating), releases FXENT_LOCK and returns. Otherwise it evaluates first_32: he_size > 0, the source is high quality, more than one pool is active and the source's pool-0 eligibility check passes. If first_32 it takes FXENT_LOCK; if the source has already given FXENT_HI_SRC_POOL0_BYTES bytes it goes to the round-robin step, else it computes rem = MIN(remaining budget, he_size), adds rem to fxrng_reseed_seen[src], hashes the last rem bytes of the entropy into pool 0, and if rem equals he_size also hashes the counter, releases the lock and returns; otherwise it reduces he_size by rem and goes to round robin. If not first_32 it takes FXENT_LOCK. Round robin: it picks pool = he_destination % fxent_nactpools, hashes the entropy (he_size bytes) and the counter into it, and for a high-quality source while the root generation is still 0 adds he_size to fxrng_preseed_ent with the same overflow guard, then releases FXENT_LOCK and returns. Events with he_size == 0 skip the first-time and pool-0 branches (both require he_size > 0).
note: fx_pool.c:307-445. Returns 354, 376, 415, 445 (void end). Reviewer round 2 right (he_size>0 guard: zero-size events go round robin, 323, 387); round 15 right (overflow guard skips instead of saturating, 372-373, 441-442). Old prose wrongly said preseed saturates. The 'always releases FXENT_LOCK' claim kept only as listed per path; fxrng_brng_src_reseed's lock handling is taken from the in-code assertion at 353 (FXRNG_BRNG_ASSERT_NOT), not read in the callee.

name: rtsx_mmcbr_update_ios
prose: Applies the cached MMC ios settings to the Realtek card reader; returns 0 or the first nonzero error. Each ios cache field rtsx_ios_bus_width, power_mode, timing, clock and vccq is negative when its value still has to be applied. In this order: if rtsx_ios_bus_width < 0 it stores ios->bus_width in the cache and calls rtsx_set_bus_width, returning its error if nonzero; if rtsx_ios_power_mode < 0 it stores ios->power_mode and calls rtsx_bus_power_off for power_off or rtsx_bus_power_on for power_up and power_on, returning its error if nonzero; then, whether or not the previous steps ran, it sets sc->rtsx_double_clk to true and sc->rtsx_vpclk to false (these two assignments are skipped when the bus-width or power-mode step returned an error); then timing (rtsx_set_sd_timing), clock (rtsx_set_sd_clock) and vccq (rtsx_mmcbr_switch_vccq) in the same pattern. Each cache field is updated before its hardware call, so a failing step returns its error with the cache already marked as applied and the later steps are not run. If no step fails it returns 0.

Reviewer round 1 right (cache stored before hardware call, 3205, 3212, 3234, 3241, 3248); round 15 right (3229-3230 are not reached after an early bus-width or power-mode failure). name: rtwn_newstate
prose: net80211 state-change method for an rtwn vap; static int. Precondition: the caller holds the net80211 com lock (IEEE80211_LOCK(ic)) on entry. If vap->iv_bss->ni_chan is IEEE80211_CHAN_ANYC and the transition is INIT to RUN, it first calls uvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg) and returns its error at once if nonzero (com lock still held), else remembers early_newstate = 1. If the old state is IEEE80211_S_CSA it cancels the CSA beacon timeout task and clears vap->iv_csa_count (before the com lock is released). It then releases the com lock and takes the driver lock. If leaving CSA it writes 0 to R92C_TXPAUSE (unblocking Tx queues). If the old state is CSA, or the old state is RUN and the new state is not CSA, it decrements sc->vaps_running, sets the port to NOLINK, stops the IBSS TSF-sync callout for IBSS vaps, disables beaconing and station beacon, resets the TSF unless uvp->id == 0 with monitor vaps running, stops the power-mode init callout and sets power mode 0 for port 0 when IEEE80211_C_PMGT is set (without RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE), recalculates basic rates when non-monitor vaps remain, and when vaps_running equals monvaps_running stops calibration, zeroes the Rx filter maps and resets EDCA parameters, turning the link LED off only when vaps_running is 0. A RUN-to-CSA transition does not decrement vaps_running. It then handles the new state: IEEE80211_S_SCAN with no vaps running pauses the AC Tx queue; IEEE80211_S_RUN calls rtwn_run, printing a message and keeping the error on failure, and incrementing vaps_running on success; IEEE80211_S_CSA pauses the AC, MGT and HIGH Tx queues. It releases the driver lock and retakes the com lock, returns the error if rtwn_run failed, and otherwise returns 0 when the early path already ran uvp->newstate, else uvp->newstate(vap, nstate, arg).
note: if_rtwn.c:1121-1254. Reviewer round 2 right (no decrement on RUN->CSA, LED only when vaps_running==0: 1162-1164, 1215-1217); round 15 right (CSA timeout cancel and iv_csa_count clear at 1144-1152 happen before IEEE80211_UNLOCK at 1154). Original reviewer (result <= 0) right that positive errors can be returned (uvp->newstate, rtwn_run). Returns 1138, 1251, 1253. Not read: rtwn_run, rtwn_set_mode, rtwn_set_pwrmode bodies.

name: r12a_handle_c2h_report
prose: Handles a C2H (firmware-to-host) report for the RTL8812A in builds with the microcode support (RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE not defined; in the other build the function only prints a 'called' message). Precondition: buf points at the start of an Rx descriptor (struct r92c_rx_stat) and len is the total length of the buffer; sc->sc_priv is an r12a_softc. It skips the Rx descriptor (buf += sizeof(struct r92c_rx_stat), len -= the same). If fewer than 2 bytes remain it prints a 'C2H report too short' message and returns. Otherwise it subtracts 2 from len and switches on buf[0] (the command id): R12A_C2H_TX_REPORT hits KASSERT(0) (only effective with INVARIANTS; otherwise nothing further), R12A_C2H_IQK_FINISHED clears R12A_IQK_RUNNING in rs->rs_flags, and any other id prints a 'was not handled' message. Returns void.

name: r12au_attach
prose: USB attach hook for the RTL8812AU; static void. It takes sc = &uc->uc_sc and sets uc->uc_align_rx to r12au_align_rx and uc->tx_agg_desc_num to 1; sets sc->sc_flags to RTWN_FLAG_EXT_HDR (replacing, not OR-ing); fills the softc's operation hooks (channel, Tx descriptor, radiotap, RSSI, interrupt classification, Tx and C2H report handlers, ROM parsing, power on and off, LLT, calibration, beacon, temperature, aggregation, EDCA, BB/RF init, antenna selection and so on) with r12a_*, r88e_*, r92c_*, r12au_* or rtwn_nop_* functions, with the firmware reset, download-enable and power-mode or media-status hooks chosen by whether RTWN_WITHOUT_UCODE is defined; and sets the chip data: the three 5 GHz channel lists and counts, the MAC, BB, AGC and RF programming tables (rtl8812au_*), name 'RTL8812AU', fwname 'rtwn-rtl8812aufw', fwsig 0x950, page and packet-buffer counts, page size, ack timeout 0x80, Tx descriptor length, efuse and Rx DMA sizes, MACID, CAM and firmware size limits, temperature delta, beacon status registers, RCR flags, two Tx and two Rx chains and sc_ht40 = 1. It finishes by calling r12a_attach_private(sc), whose result is not checked, and returns nothing.

name: safe_attach
prose: Attach routine of the safe(4) crypto accelerator driver; returns 0 or ENXIO. It maps the register BAR (sc_sr, sc_st, sc_sh), allocates and sets up the shared IRQ with safe_intr as MPSAFE handler, obtains a crypto driver id (sc_cid), creates two DMA tags (sc_srcdmat, sc_dstdmat), allocates the packet-engine ring (sc_ring, sc_ringtop, sc_front, sc_back; zeroed, with sc_ringmtx initialized), the source and destination particle rings (sc_spring/sc_spfree and sc_dpring/sc_dpfree; zeroed), prints the chip's capabilities, resets and initializes the board (safe_reset_board, safe_init_pciregs, safe_init_board), and, when SAFE_NO_RNG is not defined and the chip reports SAFE_DEVINFO_RNG, sets SAFE_FLAGS_RNG, installs the harvest function, calls safe_rng_init and arms the sc_rngto callout. It then logs a deprecation notice and returns 0. Failures print a message and return ENXIO: no register BAR (bad), IRQ not allocated (bad1), interrupt not established (bad2), no driver id (bad3), DMA tag creation or ring allocation failure (bad4). The labels unwind in order: bad4 crypto_unregister_all, bad3 bus_teardown_intr, bad2 releases the IRQ, bad1 releases the memory BAR. The failure paths do not free all DMA tags: a failed destination-tag creation leaves sc_srcdmat created; a failed ring allocation or source-particle allocation destroys sc_srcdmat but not sc_dstdmat; a failed destination-particle allocation destroys sc_dstdmat but not sc_srcdmat; the ring and particle allocations made before the failing step are freed and sc_ringmtx destroyed where those steps are reached.

Reviewer round 15 right: sc_dstdmat leaked on ring/source-particle failure (318-319, 350-353) and sc_srcdmat leaked on destination-particle failure (364-368) and on dst tag failure (306-308). Old prose said 'unwinding' without these exceptions. PARTLY READ: lines 220-240 (softc zeroing and BAR allocation) not read.

name: sdhci_card_task
prose: Taskqueue handler that reconciles the slot's registered card state with the card-detect state; static void. Precondition: arg is a struct sdhci_slot *; pending is unused. It takes the slot lock, then tests whether a card is present with SDHCI_GET_CARD_PRESENT(slot->bus, slot). If a card is present and none is registered (MMCCAM: card_present == 0; otherwise slot->dev == NULL): with MMCCAM it sets card_present to 1, starts discovery with mmccam_start_discovery and unlocks the slot; otherwise it unlocks the slot, takes the bus topology lock, sets slot->dev to the result of device_add_child(slot->bus, 'mmc', DEVICE_UNIT_ANY) and only if that is non-NULL sets the slot as ivars and calls device_probe_and_attach (result ignored), then releases the topology lock. If no card is present and one is registered: with MMCCAM it sets card_present to 0, restarts discovery and unlocks; otherwise it sets slot->dev to NULL, removes the tuning bits from intmask and writes it to SDHCI_INT_ENABLE and SDHCI_SIGNAL_ENABLE, clears SDHCI_TUNING_ENABLED, unlocks the slot, drains the retune callout and deletes the child device under the bus topology lock. In the remaining cases (no state change) it just unlocks the slot. The slot lock is released on each of these paths. Returns void.
note: sdhci.c:681-743. Reviewer round 1 right that the MMCCAM branch differs (card_present/discovery, 699-701, 726-728), which the old prose already covered; round 15 right that non-MMCCAM present path probes only when device_add_child succeeds (705-709), and old prose omitted that. Lines 681-690 (lock and card-present test) read; SDHCI_GET_CARD_PRESENT body not read.
